title: Tennessee DACA Recipients Sue Over Driver's Licenses Denied Under New Law
excerpt: A law that took effect October 1 requires a federally authorized period of stay for a temporary license — a test DACA recipients and some work-permit holders no longer pass. Advocates sued on October 30 to block it.
body:
• Tennessee's HB6001, effective October 1, requires applicants for a temporary driver's license to show a federally authorized period of stay — which the state says DACA and an employment authorization document alone do not establish.
  • DACA recipients and some work-permit holders have been denied renewals since October 1, leaving them unable to drive legally to work or school.
  • The Tennessee Immigrant and Refugee Rights Coalition and the National Immigration Law Center sued on October 30 in Davidson County Chancery Court, asking the court to block the rule and restore the previous process.
  • Governor Bill Lee said this week he had only just become aware of the denials and has asked for clarification on how federal rule changes are affecting Tennessee law.

Renewing a driver's license, a routine errand, has become impossible for a growing number of Tennessee immigrants who are authorized by the federal government to live and work in the United States. At an October 30 news conference, the Tennessee Immigrant and Refugee Rights Coalition (TIRRC) warned that if the state keeps rejecting their applications, some affected residents could leave Tennessee entirely, The Tennessean reported.

Who is affected, exactly

The affected group is specific: recipients of Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) and certain other holders of federal work permits who hold, or are renewing, a Tennessee temporary driver's license. The law does not change the position of US citizens or permanent residents. TIRRC advocacy director Jazmin Ramirez told The Tennessean that dozens of DACA recipients and work-permit holders had reported failed renewal attempts since October 1, and that the organization was still measuring the full scope.

https://x.com/FOXNashville/status/2117028954015989817

What changed

The change comes from HB6001, a 2025 immigration law that revised Tennessee's driver's license statutes. Under the revised statute, T.C.A. 55-50-331(g), an applicant for a temporary license must provide proof of a specified period of authorized stay in the United States. The Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security, in a statement shared with The Tennessean, said DACA is a form of deferred action and does not itself confer lawful immigration status, and that an employment authorization document on its own does not establish a lawful status for a specified period. On that reading, people who previously qualified for temporary licenses no longer do.

The lawsuit, and what lawmakers are saying

TIRRC and the National Immigration Law Center filed suit in Davidson County Chancery Court on October 30, challenging the law and asking the court to block the new rule and require the state to return to its previous process for issuing temporary licenses, according to The Tennessean's earlier reporting. On the political side, Governor Bill Lee told reporters he had "just become aware" of the issue, had asked for clarification about how changes to federal rules are affecting Tennessee law, and that his office was determining its response. Democratic state Representative John Ray Clemmons condemned the denials in an October 28 news release, calling them "xenophobic" and "self-destructive economic policy."

"xenophobic" and "self-destructive economic policy"

— State Rep. John Ray Clemmons, on the license denials, October 28

What affected residents should do now

The lawsuit is pending and the rule remains in effect unless a court blocks it, so a renewal appointment today is decided under the new test. TIRRC has been hosting community discussions and virtual sessions for affected residents and is collecting reports of denials — residents who have been turned away can contact the coalition through its site for guidance and to document their case. Anyone whose temporary license is close to expiring should not assume a renewal will go through as it did last time: check your expiry date now, and allow time to arrange alternative transport to work or school if a renewal is denied.
nri_angle: Indian and other immigrant residents of Tennessee on work permits should check whether their temporary license renewal is affected before it expires.
